This looks like the Sachs et al. flow cytometry dataset, so I'm answering from the published signalling network. I didn't run any analysis on `flow.csv`.

In that network there is no direct edge between PKC and PIP3. The route that exists is PIP3 → PLCγ → DAG → PKC, so PIP3 sits upstream of PKC. PKC instead acts on PKA, Raf, Mek, Jnk and p38.

PIP3 causing PKC (B) is therefore more likely than PKC causing PIP3 (A).

ANSWER: B
